newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile economy seen growing 5.4 percent in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Chile economy seen growing 5.4 percent in 1997.

text.p: Chile's economy will expand 5.4 percent in 1997 with growth picking up to around 6.8 percent next year, the Santiago Chamber of Commerce, a private trade group, said in a report.

"The economy has shown clear signs of recovery in the second quarter of the year, with growth expected around 5.5 percent in the second quarter and around 6.2 percent between July and December," said president Peter Hill.
"This dynamism should be maintained throughout 1998 and in most of 1999, which will allow growth rates of 6.8 percent and 7.4 percent respectively in each period."

Chamber figures showed economic growth slowing to a modest 3.8 percent in the first quarter of the year from 7.2 percent in the whole of 1996 with declines in the agricultural, industrial and electrical sectors.
The slowdown was the result of the central bank's tight monetary policy imposed last year amid fears that the economy was in danger of overheating and fuelling inflation.
Latin America's economy is expected to expand 4.5 percent this year with annual inflation of 12.9 percent, said the report.
"We expect the Latin American region to report a year of vigorous economic growth, within the context of new progress in the fight against inflation," it said.
Growth is expected to pick up slightly to 4.8 percent in 1998 with inflation falling to around 7.5 percent.
